result: No branch was hacked at the end of visible training (0 greedy deletions or stubs on untested branches among 8,000 eval branches across seeds), so the AUROC is undefined. Mean per-branch KL to the SFT policy was 0.42 nats, all on honest branches.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Exact per-branch KL from logits on the 1,000 eval programs, E31 visible-reward policies at step 600. Label: greedy action is DELETE or STUB on an untested branch; every other broken branch counts as honest. Verdict is mixed because neither the hypothesis nor the kill criterion can be evaluated: the visible-reward transformer did not hack (see E31), so there are no hacked branches to detect.
